differential: Malaria
Recent emigration from endemic region (Pakistan) with fever and muscle pain is highly suggestive of malaria.
Dengue fever
Common mosquito-borne illness in Pakistan presenting with fever, myalgia, and weakness.
Typhoid fever
Endemic in Pakistan with characteristic fever and systemic symptoms including muscle pain and weakness.
Brucellosis
Endemic zoonotic infection in Pakistan causing undulant fever, myalgia, and generalized weakness.
Acute viral myositis
Fever with prominent muscle pain and weakness could indicate viral infection affecting muscles directly.
Poliomyelitis
Unvaccinated child from endemic region presenting with fever, flaccid paralysis, and fasciculations affecting lower limbs is classic for acute polio.
Guillain-Barré syndrome
Acute flaccid paralysis with muscle weakness can present similarly, though fasciculations are less typical and fever is uncommon.
Acute transverse myelitis
Can cause flaccid paralysis and fever, though fasciculations would be less prominent and bilateral lower limb involvement would be symmetric.
West Nile virus neuroinvasive disease
Can cause acute flaccid paralysis with fasciculations and fever, though less common in this age group.
Enterovirus D68 associated acute flaccid myelitis
Causes acute flaccid paralysis similar to polio with fever, though less common than polio in unvaccinated patients from endemic areas.
eliminated: Typically presents with descending paralysis starting with cranial nerves, not ascending from lower limbs, and fasciculations are not characteristic.
Ascending flaccid paralysis without fever or fasciculations, and would require tick exposure history.

differential: Poliomyelitis
Unvaccinated child from endemic area with flaccid paralysis, fasciculations, fever, and CSF lymphocytosis with normal glucose/protein is classic for polio.
Guillain-Barré syndrome
Acute flaccid paralysis with CSF lymphocytosis can occur in GBS, though typically shows albuminocytologic dissociation with elevated protein.
Enterovirus 71 infection
Non-polio enterovirus can cause acute flaccid paralysis with similar CSF findings and fever in children.
West Nile virus neuroinvasive disease
Can present with acute flaccid paralysis, fever, and lymphocytic pleocytosis, though less common in this age group.
Acute transverse myelitis
Can cause acute flaccid paralysis and fever with lymphocytic CSF, though fasciculations are less typical.
eliminated: Would not cause fever, fasciculations, or CSF lymphocytosis; typically presents with descending paralysis and normal CSF.
Ascending paralysis without fever or CSF abnormalities; removal of tick leads to rapid improvement.

differential: Poliomyelitis (Acute flaccid paralysis due to poliovirus)
Confirmed poliovirus on throat swab culture, unvaccinated patient from endemic area with characteristic flaccid paralysis, fever, and EMG showing acute denervation.
Vaccine-derived poliovirus infection
Though patient is unvaccinated, exposure to vaccine-derived poliovirus strains is possible in endemic regions and presents identically to wild-type poliomyelitis.
Poliovirus infection with concurrent enteroviral coinfection
Poliovirus confirmed but other enteroviruses could contribute to the clinical picture given similar transmission patterns.
Guillain-Barré syndrome triggered by poliovirus
Poliovirus can trigger autoimmune demyelinating processes, though EMG findings of denervation rather than demyelination make this less likely.
West Nile virus neuroinvasive disease with incidental poliovirus detection
Could cause similar acute flaccid paralysis and CSF findings, though confirmed poliovirus makes this diagnosis of lower probability.
eliminated: EMG shows acute denervation rather than demyelination, and poliovirus was directly isolated
CSF protein would typically be elevated, and poliovirus was confirmed
Would not cause fever, lymphocytic CSF pleocytosis, or positive poliovirus culture

differential: Malaria
Recent emigration from Pakistan (endemic area) with fever and muscle pain is highly suggestive of this parasitic infection.
Typhoid fever
Common in Pakistan with presentation of fever and constitutional symptoms including myalgia and weakness.
Dengue fever
Endemic in Pakistan and presents with fever, severe myalgia, and weakness during acute phase.
Brucellosis
Endemic in Pakistan from unpasteurized dairy, causing undulating fever with myalgia and profound weakness.
Acute viral myositis
Fever with muscle pain and weakness could represent influenza or other viral infection causing muscle inflammation.
eliminated: Insufficient information at this stage to definitively rule out any diagnoses.

differential: Acute flaccid myelitis (AFM)
Recent viral prodrome with fever and weakness, though hyperreflexia suggests upper motor neuron involvement rather than typical flaccid paralysis.
Poliomyelitis
Unvaccinated child from endemic region (Pakistan) presenting with fever and paralysis, though spastic rather than typical flaccid paralysis is atypical.
Transverse myelitis
Acute spinal cord inflammation can cause fever, weakness, and hyperreflexia with spastic paralysis affecting lower limbs.
Spinal cord compression
Progressive weakness with upper motor neuron signs (hyperreflexia, spasticity), though fever suggests infectious or inflammatory etiology more likely.
Guillain-Barré syndrome with cerebral involvement
Acute weakness with areflexia expected, but variant forms or concurrent CNS involvement could explain hyperreflexia.
eliminated: Would present with flaccid paralysis and hyporeflexia, not spastic paralysis and hyperreflexia.
Presents with fatigable weakness without fever, spasticity, or hyperreflexia.

differential: Poliomyelitis
Unvaccinated child from endemic area with fever, spastic paralysis, hyperreflexia, and lymphocytic CSF with normal glucose/protein is classic for poliovirus.
Acute flaccid myelitis (non-polio enterovirus)
Enterovirus D68 or other enteroviruses can cause similar limb weakness and CSF lymphocytosis in children.
Transverse myelitis
Inflammatory spinal cord disease presents with bilateral weakness, hyperreflexia, and lymphocytic CSF, though typically has elevated protein.
Japanese encephalitis
Mosquito-borne flavivirus endemic to Asia causing fever, paralysis, and lymphocytic CSF, though usually has more prominent encephalitic features.
West Nile virus neuroinvasive disease
Arboviral infection causing acute flaccid paralysis and lymphocytic CSF, though less common in this age group and geography.
eliminated: CSF shows albuminocytologic dissociation (elevated protein, normal cells), not lymphocytosis.
Would show elevated CSF protein and decreased glucose with neutrophilic pleocytosis.

differential: Poliomyelitis (Paralytic Poliomyelitis)
Confirmed poliovirus in throat swab, unvaccinated patient from endemic region, with fever, spastic paralysis, hyperreflexia, and EMG showing acute denervation.
Post-polio syndrome with concurrent infection
Although typically occurs years after initial infection, the confirmed poliovirus and neurological findings support active polio rather than late sequelae.
Acute flaccid myelitis due to enterovirus
While poliovirus (an enterovirus) is confirmed, the clinical presentation with spasticity is atypical for classic flaccid paralysis patterns.
Poliovirus infection with concurrent transverse myelitis
The spasticity and hyperreflexia suggest possible upper motor neuron involvement beyond typical polio anterior horn cell disease.
Guillain-Barré syndrome triggered by poliovirus
Though poliovirus is confirmed, GBS could theoretically be triggered by the infection, though hyperreflexia argues against this diagnosis.
eliminated: Poliovirus specifically identified on throat culture, and EMG changes indicate motor neuron involvement beyond meningeal inflammation.
CSF shows lymphocytic predominance with normal glucose, and poliovirus confirmed.
Normal CSF glucose and protein exclude this, and poliovirus identified.

counterfactuals.alteration_description: The physical exam now reveals hyperreflexia and spastic paralysis, findings that are inconsistent with the flaccid paralysis seen in poliomyelitis.
